variants.headline: Builder left unpaid for work done
variants.sub: The builder {builder} is owed payment by the client {client} for completed work.
variants.body:
The client {client} has not paid the builder {builder} for work done. The amount owed is {owed}. After three missed months the builder stops work. For {target}, the event raises the basic question of responsibility when a construction undertaking requires payment as well as performance.

Work done is work that deserves a serious account of payment. Labour should keep that connection visible without making an employer's receipt the whole measure of a worker's life. A missed obligation is a proper subject of scrutiny, not something to disappear behind a tidy description of construction progress.

We support {target} against a blanket adverse verdict. The missed payment requires attention, but its existence does not prove every allegation about motives or establish that the project has already reached a stop. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.

variants.headline: A construction payment fails to arrive
variants.sub: Payment for work done by {builder} has been missed by {client}.
